# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Mary Stubbs, having been dispatched to the manse on a chore by Mrs. Kerr, was walking lightly down Fern Hollow, heading to Hollowmere to pass the afternoon alongside Bess and Izzy for a Saturday reward. Grace and Ida had joined Bess and Izzy to gather spruce gum within the woods of the manse, and the quartet sat presently upon a collapsed pine alongside the stream, each one, it should be acknowledged, masticating quite energetically. Anywhere outside the privacy of Fern Hollow, the Hollowmere twins were forbidden from chewing spruce gum, whereas Grace and Ida remained unconstrained by those etiquette regulations and happily masticated it all over, both in the house and outside, causing the Glen to feel a most respectable dread. Indeed, Grace had masticated it during a church service on a single occasion; nevertheless, Tobias recognized how monstrous that was, administering a lecture in the manner of a big brother that proved so severe she refrained from ever repeating the act.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0000 }

“I felt such a need to chew on something because my hunger was so great,” she argued. “Tobias Ashdown, you are fully aware of the nature of our breakfast. Burnt porridge was impossible for me to consume, leaving my stomach feeling exceedingly odd and hollow. That gum was a great aid—plus I refrained from chewing forcefully. No sound came from me, and not a single time did I pop the gum.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0001 }

“Anyhow, chewing gum in church is something you mustn’t do,” Tobias insisted. “If I catch you doing it again, you’ll be sorry.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0002 }

“During prayer-meeting last week, you chewed yourself,” Grace shouted.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0003 }

“That’s different,” Tobias stated haughtily. “Prayer-meeting isn’t on Sunday. Besides, I sat far in the rear in a shadowy pew and no one noticed me. You were seated right in the front where all the people noticed you. And I removed the gum from my mouth for the final hymn and attached it to the rear of the pew right in the front where all the people noticed you. Then I departed and left it behind. I returned to retrieve it the following morning, but it had vanished. I imagine Rod Warren stole it. And it was a dandy chew.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0004 }

Mary Stubbs moved along the Valley with her head lifted proudly. She was wearing a fresh blue velvet cap that featured a scarlet rosette, a coat made of navy blue cloth, and a small muff of squirrel fur. She was extremely aware of her fresh garments and immensely satisfied with her appearance. Her hair had been meticulously crimped, her face appeared rather full, her cheeks were rosy, and her white eyes were gleaming. She bore little resemblance to the miserable and tattered stray whom the Ashdowns had discovered inside the old Taylor barn. Ida attempted to keep envy at bay. In this moment stood Mary wearing a fresh velvet cap, whereas she and Grace were required to put on their faded old gray tams once more this winter. No one ever considered purchasing new ones for them, and they feared requesting them from their father because he might be lacking funds, which would cause him to feel distressed. Mary had mentioned to them on one occasion that ministers were constantly lacking funds and found it “awful hard” to make ends meet. From that time on, Grace and Ida preferred wearing rags over requesting anything from their father if they could avoid doing so. They did not feel overly troubled by their worn appearance; nevertheless, it proved somewhat difficult to observe Mary Stubbs stepping out in such fashion and exhibiting such arrogance over it, as well. The fresh squirrel muff truly served as the final indignity. Neither Grace nor Ida had ever owned a muff, considering themselves fortunate if they managed to secure mittens devoid of holes. Aunt Martha lacked the eyesight required to mend holes, and even though Ida attempted the task, she produced clumsy mending. For some reason, they were unable to render their welcome to Mary particularly warm. However, Mary remained unbothered and unaware of this, as she was not excessively thin-skinned. She leaped nimbly onto a perch on the pine tree, placing the disagreeable muff upon a branch. Ida observed that its lining consisted of gathered red satin and it possessed red tassels. She stared down at her own somewhat purple, rough, tiny hands and pondered whether she would ever, ever have the chance to slide them inside a muff of that sort.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0005 }

“Give us a chew,” Mary requested in a friendly tone. Bess, Izzy and Grace each pulled one or two amber-colored lumps out of their pockets, handing them over to Mary. Ida did not move at all. Inside the pocket of her snug, worn-out small jacket rested four splendid, large lumps, yet she refused to hand even a single one over to Mary Stubbs—absolutely none. Mary could gather her own gum! Owners of squirrel muffs should not anticipate receiving every single thing in existence.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0006 }

“Isn’t it a great day?” Mary remarked, dangling her legs, possibly to show off her new boots that featured quite stylish cloth tops. Ida pulled her own feet beneath herself. A hole was present in the toe of one boot, and numerous knots bound both of her laces. Nevertheless, she possessed no better pair. Oh, that Mary Stubbs! Why had she not been left behind in the old barn?
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0007 }

Ida was never made to feel unhappy because the Hollowmere twins had finer garments than Grace and she possessed. With an indifferent elegance, they bore their lovely attire, appearing never to bestow a thought upon it. In some manner, they refrained from causing those around them to feel dowdy. However, whenever Mary Stubbs was finely attired, she appeared almost to radiate garments—to move within an aura of garments—to force everyone else into feeling and thinking garments. As Ida remained seated in the golden warmth of the pleasant December afternoon, she was sharply and wretchedly aware of every single item she wore—the discolored tam, which remained her finest one nevertheless, the ill-fitting jacket that had served her across three winters, the frayed areas in her skirt and her footwear, and the chilly inadequacy of her meager little underclothing. Naturally, Mary was preparing to go visiting whereas she remained behind. Yet even had she been departing as well, no superior clothes were hers to wear, and the sharpness of her distress rested in this fact.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0008 }

“Hey, this gum is wonderful. Hear me popping it. Down at Seven Gulls, there aren't any gum spruces,” Mary stated. “At times, I simply crave a chew. If Mrs. Kerr spots me, she forbids me from chewing gum. She claims it isn't lady-like. I am confused by this lady-business. I am unable to understand all its quirks. Hey, Ida, what is wrong with you? Has the cat got your tongue?”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0009 }

“No,” uttered Ida, whose transfixed gaze remained glued to the squirrel muff. Reaching across her, Mary snatched the item up and shoved it directly into Ida’s hands.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0010 }

“Put your hands inside there for a moment,” she commanded. “They seem somewhat cold. Isn't that an exquisite muff? Mrs. Kerr presented it to me a week ago as a gift for my birthday. I will receive the collar when Christmas comes. I overheard her saying that to Mr. Kerr.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0011 }

“Grace remarked that Mrs. Kerr was extremely kind to me.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0012 }

“You can be sure she is. Plus, I treat her well,” Mary shot back. “I labor tirelessly so things are simple for her and set up precisely to her taste. We were a perfect match. Not just anybody could manage to live with her the way I can. She is obsessively clean, but I am the same way, which makes us get on great.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0013 }

“I informed you that she was never going to whip you.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0014 }

“That is true. She has never attempted to put a finger on me, and I have never uttered a single falsehood to her—not a single one, as sure as you live. However, she scolds me with her tongue on occasion, but that merely slides off me like water off a duck’s back. Tell me, Ida, why did you not keep the muff?”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0015 }

Ida had restored it to the branch.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0016 }

“I do not have cold hands, thank you,” she stated frostily.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0017 }

“Well, if you are satisfied, I am. Tell me, old Kitty Hector has returned to church as humble as Moses and no one understands the reason. But everyone is claiming it was Grace who brought Lionel Fairlie out. His housekeeper states that you visited there and delivered a terrible tongue-lashing to him. Did you?”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0018 }

“I walked over and requested that he join us at church,” Grace mentioned uneasily.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0019 }

“Imagine having such nerve!” Mary remarked with admiration. “I wouldn’t have ventured to do that, and I’m hardly timid. Mrs. Wilson claims that both of you argued terribly, yet you emerged victorious, after which he simply pivoted and seemed ready to devour you. Tell me, will your father be preaching here tomorrow?”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0020 }

“No. His intention is to swap places with Mr. Perry from Port Marlow. Father traveled to town earlier today, and Mr. Perry will arrive this evening.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0021 }

“I suspected that something was going on, even if old Martha refused to tell me anything satisfactory. Nevertheless, I was certain she would not have slaughtered that rooster without a reason.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0022 }

“Which rooster? What are you talking about?” exclaimed Grace, her face losing its color.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0023 }

“I am unaware of any rooster, as I never saw it. At the time she collected the butter sent by Mrs. Kerr, she mentioned having visited the barn to slaughter a rooster for tomorrow’s dinner.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0024 }

Grace leaped from the pine tree down to the ground.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0025 }

“It’s Adam—we don’t possess any other rooster—Adam has been killed by her.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0026 }

“Now, don’t lose your temper. Martha mentioned that no meat was available from the butcher at the Glen this week, forcing her to find an alternative, and since the hens were all laying, they were too scrawny.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0027 }

“In the event that she has murdered Adam—” Grace started rushing up the incline.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0028 }

Mary gave a shrug of her shoulders.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0029 }

“She will lose her mind now. Her affection for that Adam was immense. That bird should have been cooked a long time back—his meat will be as hard as sole leather. However, I would hate to be in Martha’s position. Grace has turned completely pale from anger; Ida, it would be wise for you to follow her and attempt to calm her down.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0030 }

Ida abruptly spun around and sprinted toward Mary just as she had walked a short distance alongside the Carrow girls.
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0031 }

“Mary, here is some gum for you,” she said, her voice catching slightly in repentance, as she shoved every one of her four knots into Mary’s hands, “and it makes me happy that your muff is so pretty.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0032 }

“Why, thanks,” Mary said, feeling somewhat astonished. Once Ida had left, she remarked to the Carrow girls, “Ain’t she a queer little mite? But I’ve always said she had a good heart.”
{: #nw-v05-c18-p0033 }
